title: Sterling Bluff Plant Call: "Noon Reopen?" — PHC 0.62 at the Intake

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Water Plant Control Room

caller.name: Dale Hendricks
caller.label: Plant Superintendent, Sterling Bluff Water Department

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: Boss, it's Dale. Got a minute? Because I don't think we have many. Storage is down to 4.1 million gallons. Even with conservation and the wells at full output, we're drawing a net of about a third of a million an hour once you count the half million a day going out the interconnect to the rural district. That gives us roughly twelve hours. Call it nine-thirty tonight.

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: Now the river. I pulled a raw-water grab at the intake at 08:30. No visible sheen. But the field screen reads petroleum hydrocarbons 0.62 milligrams per liter, and our action level is 0.5. TOC is 3.4, up from 2.1 yesterday morning. And my operator says there's a faint odor, kind of diesel-sweet. Next grab is at 09:30.

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: And one more thing, from the Prairie Spill crew on the bank. A boom upstream at mile 31 let go overnight, and there's a fresh sheen coming down the left bank toward us. So 'the oil has passed' isn't something I'd sign.

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: The City Manager just copied me on an email to you, subject 'Reopen today?' I'll read it: 'The Mayor wants the intake open by noon and a press line at 10:00 saying the oil has passed and Sterling Bluff water is safe. Ironbark's liaison says the river looks clean at mile 34.' End quote. So, what do you want me to do with the gate?

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: Hang on. I've got KDHE Bureau of Water on the other line. I'm bringing her in.

transcript.speaker: KDHE Bureau of Water Engineer
transcript.text: Director, this is Priya Natarajan, KDHE Bureau of Water. I'm hearing talk of a noon reopening. To be clear, we have not concurred with anything. Send me your plant results, including this morning's grabs, and the Environmental Unit's written recommendation before anyone touches that gate. I'll also need to know what you're doing for the dialysis center, the medical center and the nursing homes if storage gets tight.

transcript.speaker: KDHE Bureau of Water Engineer
transcript.text: And please make sure nobody on the city side uses the word 'safe' in a release unless my bureau has agreed to it. When can I have your numbers?

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: Boss, last thing. Our PIO in the JIC just forwarded this from the county chat. The County EM PIO is asking whether Ironbark's PIO can, quote, 'just put oil has passed, water safe in the 10:00 joint release. The Commissioner's asking.' Ironbark's liaison is standing right here nodding.

transcript.speaker: Plant Superintendent
transcript.text: Also, the dialysis center's charge nurse called at 08:50 about this afternoon's shift. She wants to know if she should be worried about pressure or quantity. Nobody's called her back yet. So: gate, Mayor, press line, dialysis. Tell me which order.

voiceStyles.Plant Superintendent: Man in his 50s, tired after an all-night shift, steady but clipped, plant pumps humming behind him
voiceStyles.KDHE Bureau of Water Engineer: Woman in her 40s, calm, precise, regulatory tone, quiet office

instructorNote: This is pressure to reopen early on a failed sample (PHC 0.62 against 0.5, odor) while the boom at mile 31 has failed upstream. SBWD should keep the gate closed under Water Department plan section 4 (EU recommendation, KDHE concurrence and clean plant tests), extend conservation and call the dialysis center, the medical center and the nursing homes directly. ENVL should not make a reopen recommendation, and PIO should refuse "safe", refer drinking-water status to the utility and KDHE, and clear wording through the JIC.
